claims.explanation: Carmofur's selectivity is best explained by its dual inhibition of thymidylate synthase (TYMS) and acid ceramidase (ASAH1), with additional contributions from oxidative stress and ceramide-mediated apoptosis. Lines with high TYMS expression or ASAH1 expression are more dependent on these enzymes and thus more sensitive, while mutations in DNA repair and chromatin remodeling genes may further modulate response.

features.basis: carmofur is a TYMS inhibitor; high TYMS expression may predict sensitivity
carmofur inhibits acid ceramidase (ASAH1); high expression may confer sensitivity
TP53 mutations are common in sensitive lines and may impair DNA damage response
SMARCA4 mutations are enriched in sensitive lines, possibly altering chromatin and drug response
ARID1A mutations appear in several sensitive lines, linking chromatin remodeling to sensitivity
KMT2C mutations are present in multiple sensitive lines, suggesting a role in drug response
KMT2D mutations are observed in sensitive lines, possibly affecting transcriptional regulation
BRAF mutations are found in several sensitive lines, including thyroid and glioma
NRAS mutations appear in sensitive lines such as SKNSH and KU1919
CTNNB1 mutations are present in multiple sensitive lines, including U2OS and HEC265
KEAP1 mutation in HEC265 may impair oxidative stress response, enhancing carmofur-induced ROS
NFE2L2 mutations in some resistant lines may upregulate antioxidant pathways, reducing carmofur-induced oxidative stress
